dramatic_truth: White Span's wrong-direction dawn reflection is observed under clean witness discipline, making the phenomenon stranger by behaving like an ordinary reflection attached to impossible geometry.
performance: Greg records only what the river actually does, resists fish-story inference, distinguishes administrative ferry holds from physical effects, and lets local operators own bridge procedure.
screenplay: Pre-dawn approach; west-bank witness positions; false west-facing sunrise appears while real sun remains east; bucketed water loses effect; bridge shadow does not fully extinguish band; duration logged; local ferryman theories remain unproven.
prose_comparison: The observational density is the scene's dramatic engine. Removing repeated measurements would collapse the distinction between anomaly and explanation.

dramatic_truth: Westbank market turns Greg's growing capital discipline toward a cheap retired current-reader that is useful because its failure modes and maintenance needs are legible.
performance: He asks for a demonstration, learns rain/oil/soap/mud and expectation can distort readings, buys one small tool instead of treating every river artifact as destiny, and keeps it supplemental to local authority.
screenplay: Riva demonstrates WS-F/9 treated slate in tray; one-copper purchase includes renewal rub; Sori and Vessa inspect retirement status; next White Span comparison adds wind and isolated-basin controls.
prose_comparison: Shopping detail changes Greg's toolkit and his spending logic while preserving scale. It is not repetitive acquisition fantasy.

dramatic_truth: A second White Span dawn under choppier wind tests whether the wrong reflection depends on calm river geometry rather than simply replaying the anomaly.
performance: Greg treats absence, sheltered patches, basin comparison, and wind change as separate evidence and keeps his personal slate reader subordinate to Fenner's local test plan.
screenplay: Wind/chop baseline; cleaned basin beside river; same witness positions; false reflection changes form under disturbed surface; local comparisons narrow conditions without proving mechanism.
prose_comparison: The second morning is a changed-variable experiment, not repeated spectacle.

dramatic_truth: Bellweather's old mirror infrastructure and forty-two years of records provide a comparison case that makes White Span's anomaly more local, recent, or geometry-dependent without supplying a neat answer.
performance: Greg and Dask use indexes, keeper demonstrations, and healthy old plate behavior to compare categories while resisting the urge to call every directional optical effect the same phenomenon.
screenplay: Bellweather archive search; ordinary glare/double-dawn incidents separated from persistent wrong reflection; old dawn/lamp mirror arrays examined under keeper control; no matching historical case found.
prose_comparison: The archive and mirror detail performs comparative falsification. Compressing it to 'Bellweather had no match' would erase why that conclusion is trustworthy.

dramatic_truth: Travel toward Sable Quay turns prior river observation into paid regional competence while Greg's body continues recovering and the market horizon widens substantially.
performance: He keeps mobility limits explicit, uses ordinary road systems instead of improvising, and arrives at a much larger commercial center without treating every visible device as purchase pressure.
screenplay: Road out of Bellweather; Low Fen Orchard rest; Sable Quay approach; freight-control split delays crew cases; Greg's party walks in while Kel holds animals; regional Survey Annex receives their observation packet.
prose_comparison: The route changes scale, geography, and economic context. Travel detail is state transfer, not scenic padding.

dramatic_truth: A Dock Eight contract pays Greg to inspect transfer-frame behavior, proving his bounded observation skill has direct commercial value even when the equipment problem belongs to dock specialists.
performance: He and the crew keep B's known failure separate from C's intermittent hitch, accept cleaning as maintenance rather than magic diagnosis, and Greg performs a controlled lever add-on without anticipating the machine.
screenplay: Frames A/B/C independent visual and unloaded comparisons; C's hitch appears intermittently and clears after guide cleaning; Greg runs A control cycles under Bran; four copper paid; Nema announces salvage auction.
prose_comparison: Repeated frame cycles are comparative evidence and directly justify the contract result and later auction valuation.

dramatic_truth: Greg bids at the Dock Eight auction, loses deliberately at his pre-set ceiling, then chooses Duskport with his own money and no assignment pushing him onward.
performance: He refuses auction-loss psychology, spends zero on salvage, then converts a voluntary desire to see farther into a three-copper packet ticket while explicitly telling home that this part is his choice.
screenplay: Auction lots; Greg stops at ceiling on mixed hardware; post-auction crew choices diverge; Maro, Dask, Sori, Greg buy Duskport deck tickets; Vessa/Kel stay; Greg writes home.
prose_comparison: The chapter is about ownership of choice. Bidding and travel purchase are distinct decisions with different emotional stakes.

dramatic_truth: On Bright Gull, Tessa Morn's sick-son emergency forces Greg to confront a case where procedure protects many people but cannot make every remaining choice feel humane.
performance: He does not seize captain authority; instead he asks routing questions until a private fisher at the scheduled Mile House stop can carry Tessa onward without derailing the packet, while accepting her anger that help did not come sooner.
screenplay: Tessa asks repeated crew for Reedbank deviation; captain refuses unscheduled shallow cut; Greg/Sori/Maro clarify stakes; Mile House fisher Noll can reach Reedbank before dark; Tessa leaves packet under her own risk; no success is guaranteed.
prose_comparison: The repeated requests make the moral pressure visible. The scene's point is not clever routing but the insufficiency of procedure when human costs remain.

dramatic_truth: A Gate Nine delay forces passengers with incompatible urgent needs to negotiate who should absorb the cost of priority, pushing Greg beyond uncertainty discipline into mediation under real tradeoffs.
performance: Greg asks for actual prices and incentives, surfaces captain route-review risk, lets Harven and Mira state their own stakes, and resists turning himself into moral authority while still helping facts become actionable.
screenplay: Night queue; Harven fears missing daughter's hearing; Mira risks bird quarantine and farm debt; priority pricing and route incentives clarified; passengers/captain evaluate options while queue changes; Duskport arrival preserves unresolved human consequences.
prose_comparison: Dialogue repetition is conflict calibration, not redundant arguing. Each new fact changes whose sacrifice looks reasonable.

dramatic_truth: Duskport turns Greg's growing money into a concrete mobility prospect: a real work limb could return hands and carrying capacity, but the twenty-copper deposit would leave him almost cashless.
performance: He asks what he actually wants from a limb, accepts that crutches remain part of life, refuses a deposit that would leave one copper, and learns a possible work path at Venn Marine Recovery instead of forcing the purchase.
screenplay: Arrival and cheap lodging; first current-life ocean view; Hark & Venn mobility shop; Masta Venn assesses below-knee stump and prices basic/travel/marine options; Greg declines immediate deposit; condition-clerk work lead appears through Venn Marine Recovery.
prose_comparison: The long assessment converts disability, money, work, and future optionality into one concrete decision. 'Possible enough to hurt' is new state, not repeated shopping.
